_note: The first-30-minutes tutorial. Each goal's check is in src/ui/tutorial.ts, keyed by id. {name} is the deputy. welcome is the card every new game opens with (src/view/welcome.ts); **bold** marks emphasis, {colonists} is the landing party's size.

welcome.title: Welcome to Mars, Administrator.
paragraphs: Earth sent you here to build something that lasts: a home where people can live for generations.

There's a catch. Mars has almost no air and no magnetic field, so radiation from the Sun and deep space hits the surface unchecked. Stay up there too long, even in a suit or rover, and it catches up with you.
You have **{colonists} colonists**, enough supplies to get started, and **one very large drill**. As it bores into the ground, you'll carve homes, farms and workshops into the walls of the hole.
It's the only way to live here for good. Let's dig in.
welcome.guidedButton: I'm new to games like this
welcome.guidedNote: Your deputy walks you through it one step at a time, with the game slowed down and no surprises.

_guided: The guided tutorial (F-007, T-083), picked on the welcome card for newcomers to city builders. One step at a time, in order. check: a goal id from src/ui/tutorialGoals.ts CHECKS (none: the step is read, and the player clicks the button to go on). unlocks: the UI elements the step reveals (hud:<id> from view/hudItems.ts HUD_IDS, mode:<build|view|charts|map>, room:<id>, overlay:<type>, tool:<id>), recorded in the save for T-084 to hide the rest. pace: slow (the game runs at config slowSpeed) or read (paused until the button). clip: an optional "Show me" clip (T-086). Storms and events wait until calmUntil's step is done. These are placeholders; T-085 writes the real steps.

guided.intro: I'm {name}, your deputy. I'll show you around one thing at a time, and I've slowed things down so nothing runs away from us.

steps.text: First, time. Up top are the speed buttons: pause, and faster. While we're learning I'll keep things slow, and pause when there's something to read.
steps.hint: Space pauses and unpauses. You can speed up whenever you like.

steps.text: Twenty people and nowhere to cook. Let's build a galley in ring 1, right on the shaft.
steps.hint: Click Build at the bottom right, then Food, then the galley, and click a free slot in ring 1.

steps.text: Next, a restroom. People like one within a short walk of home.
steps.hint: In Build, pick the restroom and place it in ring 1.

guided.outro: That's the start of a colony. There's more to learn; for now, keep digging.

intro: I'm {name}, your deputy. Twenty of us, one pod, and a hole that goes nowhere yet. Let's make it a home.

goals.text: Twenty people and nowhere to cook. Put a galley in ring 1, on the shaft.
goals.hint: Press B for Build, then G for a galley (or Build, bottom right, then Food), and click a free slot in ring 1. A kitchen plus a canteen does the same job.

goals.text: Next, a restroom. Homes within a short walk of one are more comfortable.
goals.hint: In Build (B), press W and place it in ring 1.

goals.text: We breathe out CO2. A CO2 scrubber turns it back into oxygen. It's loud, so put it in ring 2, behind the rooms on the shaft.
goals.hint: In Build (B), press L. It takes 4 slots; R rotates it. It won't run until a corridor reaches it: that's next.

goals.text: Rooms past ring 1 need a corridor back to the shaft. Carve one along the borders between rooms, out from the gallery.
goals.hint: In Build, press Z and drag along the borders, or click Connect in a cut-off room's panel.

goals.text: Every room we dig is new space to fill with air. An electrolyzer splits water into oxygen, and only runs when the air needs it.
goals.hint: In Build (B), open Air and pick the electrolyzer. It takes 2 slots; ring 2 is fine.

goals.text: Earth ships water, and it has to go somewhere. A water tank holds 200.
The pod is cramped. Build a bunk dorm somewhere quiet.
goals.hint: In Build (B), press D. While placing, the status bar shows the noise a spot already has.

goals.text: Check your work: turn on the noise overlay. Red is where people won't sleep.
goals.hint: View, at the bottom right, then Noise under Overlay.

goals.text: We're running. Speed things up and wait for Earth's first supply drop.
Rations won't last forever. Build two farms and grow different crops: potatoes and soybeans make a start.
goals.hint: In Build (B), press F. Click a farm to change its crop. Farms need soil, water, power and CO2.

goals.text: Someone's waiting at the office. Hear them out: people remember how you treat them.
goals.hint: Click Office in the top bar.

goals.text: Water keeps vanishing. Open Flows to see where it goes.
goals.hint: Charts, at the bottom right, then Flows and the Water tab.

goals.text: Most of it goes down the drain as gray water. A water recycler brings it back.
goals.hint: In Build (B), press Y. It needs metal and machinery from Earth.

goals.text: Last one: a clinic keeps people healthy and makes the neighborhood feel safer.
Now step back and look at what you've built: switch to the 3D view and try Cutaway to see every ring.
goals.hint: View, at the bottom right, then Cutaway. Drag to look around; Plan or Unrolled to come back.

outro: That's a working colony. From here, every colonist we can support is a point on the board. Keep digging.
_tips: Tips (F-018, T-177): a one-time deputy card the first time one of a tip's causes shows up (src/view/tips.ts), in data order. causes are diagnosis causes (data/diagnosis.json) as health:<id> (anything draining the hole's health) or happiness:<id> (costing happiness tipPoints or more). None before fromDay. Seen tips are kept in the save; Settings > Tips turns them off. {name} is the deputy.

tips.text: Smell and stale air ride the corridors, the way they would in a ship. That's what bulkheads are for: a sealed door on a corridor stops them getting past.
tips.hint: In Build (B), press Z for corridors, then pick Bulkhead and click the corridor between the smelly rooms (galleys, farms, composters, smelters) and the homes. Show me lights up who's making it and who's feeling it.

tips.text: People need a restroom within a short walk of home. Fewer than half with one and the hole's health starts to slide.
tips.hint: In Build (B), press W. Put restrooms near the homes: about 6 steps at most.

tips.text: We're breathing out more CO2 than we take back, and above 1% of the air it starts making people ill.
tips.hint: In Build (B), press L for a CO2 scrubber. Farms breathe it in too. Both need power.

tips.text: The air's getting thin. Below 18% oxygen people start to suffer.
tips.hint: An electrolyzer (in Build, under Air) splits water into oxygen; a CO2 scrubber turns CO2 back into it. Every room you dig is more air to fill.

tips.text: People are going hungry. They eat only cooked meals: rations and crops need a galley or kitchen to cook them.
tips.hint: In Build (B), press G for a galley. Farms grow raw food for it; Earth sends rations.

tips.text: We're short of water, and people get ill without it.
tips.hint: A water recycler brings gray water back; tanks hold more of what Earth sends. Flows (under Charts) shows where it goes.

tips.text: Some homes have no clinic within reach. Knowing help is close makes people feel safer.
tips.hint: In Build (B), press K. A clinic covers homes within about 10 steps; a bigger one reaches further.

tips.text: Some people have nowhere to sit down to eat near home. Each galley seats so many, within a short walk.
tips.hint: Another galley or a canteen near the homes, or a bigger one.

tips.text: Homes are crowded: too many people sharing the air in too little space.
tips.hint: More homes, so fewer share each one. Roomier homes (studios, flats) help too.

tips.text: Noise is keeping people up. It travels through rock to the rooms around it, but stops at a corridor.
tips.hint: Move noisy rooms (scrubbers, pumps, workshops) away from homes or put a corridor between them. The Noise overlay (View) shows where it reaches.
